about: hi. i program games on my ti-83 plus and sell them for $2. i have 5 titles, all in ti-basic, all under 4 kb: SNAKE+, BLOCKFALL, PYRAMID ESCAPE, CAVE DIVER and a custom order i dont talk about yet. transfer is by link cable, 11 seconds per game. cable rental is 50 cents. batteries (4 aaa, $4.99) are my biggest expense and yes i have a spreadsheet for that too. i keep a ledger. i started it in 7th grade and it has never been wrong, which is not the same as never being sad. im on the math team (11th of 14 at regionals, up from 13th). no refunds. feedback is accepted and costs nothing. its the only free thing here.
aboutMore: things to know before doing business. 1) prices are posted and they do not change when you cry. 2) i dont sell answers, cheats, or anything that helps on a test. the quadratic solver is for me. 3) i sell off campus only. the late bus is technically off campus. mr henderson and i have agreed to disagree about the bus. 4) my sister maya (9) was customer #1 and has never been invoiced. she is listed under 'other.' people ask what 'other' means. it means other.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: whoever at texas instruments gave the ti-83 24 kb of ram, to say thanks and ask why not 25. a customer who reads the price before asking the price. kate bush, about the digits. the person who invented the receipt. and henry, to hand him exactly two dollars. bulletins.subject: the link cable is not a leash (an announcement)
bulletins.body: several customers have asked if they can 'just keep the cable overnight.' no. it is 2 feet long and it is my only distribution channel. when you hold it, i have no business. if you want to keep it, we can talk about a deposit, which is $5 and is returned in full when the cable is returned in full, with a receipt. i also do not rent it to people who 'will bring it back tomorrow' because that sentence has a failure rate i have measured and it is 100%.

ERR:NONREAL ANS. thats what the calculator says when you take the square root of a negative number. i find that dismissive. 'nonreal.' it has a name. its i. my math teacher says i can use it. the ledger has no use for it.

i started a pi day playlist. its one song. kate bush sings the digits and somewhere in the middle it goes wrong and i have never been able to find out why. i wrote to a fan site twice. nobody has written back. logged under 'correspondence (pending).'

a 6th grader asked me today if there was a free game. i said no. then i said let me check the ledger. then i went home and checked. there was one. i put it on her calculator. she said thanks and ran. there isnt a column for that. well. there is. never mind.

my sister maya (9) asked what a dividend is and then asked if her goldfish pays one. i said not yet. she named him Dividend anyway. he is now the only member of this household with a financial instrument for a name. i am proud and a little scared.

the vending machine in the east hall gave me an extra dime today. i walked it to the front office. debbie said 'honey, its a dime.' i said its 10 cents that is not mine. she put it in a jar on her desk labeled FOUND. the jar has $4.30 in it. thats 43 dimes from people like me, which is more people like me than i expected. i did not enter it in the ledger. i dont know which column it goes in.

blog.title: the ledger, quarterly (public edition)
blog.body: QUARTER ENDING SEPT 30. 1) games sold: 31, $58.75 after bulk. 2) cable rentals: 22, $11.00. 3) batteries: 3 packs, -$14.97. 4) lunch and snacks: -$21.10 (the cafeteria pretzel remains the best value in the building). 5) supplies: -$6.45 (graph paper, 2 pens, and a sharpener to replace the one that ate the pencil). 6) math team dues: -$5.00. NET: $22.23. a few notes. sales are up about 40% since i added the cable rental, which was not a pricing decision, it was a cable i had. category 7 is not included. category 7 is not for audit. thank you for reading. that is all.

blog.title: DENNIS DODGE: a post-mortem (refund pending)
blog.body: on sept 22 a 13 year old on wheels placed a custom order. requirements: a stick figure on wheels, a security guard who is faster than he looks, a fountain, 3 levels. price: $2.00, same as always. labor was 11 hours, which is not a billing unit i recognize. he played levels 1 and 2 and loved them. level 3 has a bug. the guard speeds up every frame and never stops. i computed your chance of surviving the fountain at about 0.3%. i should have computed it earlier. he asked for a refund. my policy is no refunds. my policy also did not account for a bug, so i wrote an exception into the price list after the fact, which is not how rules work. i have never issued a refund so i had no form. i made one. it is a post-it. current balance: -$2.00. my first red line in 12 quarters. it is the same color as the pen i used.

blog.title: category 7 (i said i would not do this one)
blog.body: my grandma balanced her checkbook to the penny every month until she was 88. i found the statements in a drawer, rubber banded, in order. i think she knew the only way to be kind with money is to know exactly where it is. thats why i have a ledger. categories 1 through 6 are on this blog. category 7 is called 'other.' this year it is -$31.40. it is a 6th grader who asked 'is there a free one' with the face. it is $5 for the pie fund on pi day. it is a goldfish bowl and a goldfish for maya. it is a spare pack of batteries i left in a bag for a kid whose died during regionals. i dont audit it. every other category i check twice. this one i write down, close the book, and put the pencil down.
